findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 1, Harm 4
Raise: Data loss
Case: normal use - An interrupted earlier train left its branch, and a later run recreates the same candidate commit, for example when Git commit dates are fixed. Git treats a push of an identical ref as up to date before checking the empty lease, as shown in [Git's push implementation](https://github.com/git/git/blob/v2.39.5/remote.c#L1608-L1629). Forge therefore sets `pushed` even though it did not create the branch, and its `finally` block deletes that existing branch; an existing pull request from it is affected too. This is new evidence beyond the collision test, which puts a different commit at the occupied name.
findings.title: Keep an existing train branch that already points at the candidate

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - A CI repo requires `lint` and `forge-pr-check`, while a separate app-test check is not required. The new guard accepts `lint` merely because its name differs from `forge-pr-check`. The generated workflow does not create its test job unless `tests` is configured (`src/forge/prcheck.py:261,425-428`), so a fast green lint result can make the train pass before the separate test check reports. Forge can then merge the combination without testing it. The earlier repair and its `no-app-check` variant cover only the list containing `forge-pr-check` alone.
Adds work: require evidence of an app-test check for the combined run; F 2 x H 2 = 4; 2 x C = 2
findings.title: A non-test check can still admit an untested train

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - Ready branches were created with `test_place = "local"`, then the default branch switched to CI before `land --all`. Train selection correctly uses the new default settings, but this shortcut skips the merge-in that would refresh each member's settings. `merge.py:102` retains the old local setting and `merge.py:162-165` consequently skips `checks.wait` when `checks.required` returns no override. If an unrequired member check turns red during the train, GitHub can merge that red member. The new evidence is the difference between the fetched default settings and the still-old settings at the member head; the added `member-red` test uses CI settings at both.
Adds work: apply the existing member check gate under the fetched settings; F 2 x H 2 = 4; 2 x C = 2
findings.title: Keep the member check gate after a switch from local tests to CI

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - An upgraded repo has a ready pull request from an earlier release, with a clean review and green checks but no local or shared `ready` receipt. `nextstep._item_readiness` accepts that evidence (`src/forge/nextstep.py:887-894`), so it enters the train. This shortcut skips close, while `merge.merge` requires a local or shared ready receipt (`src/forge/merge.py:73-84`). After the combined check passes, the member is stopped under Needs you instead of being closed and merged as in the previous land path. The adopted-repo train test creates and closes its changes with the current release, so it does not cover an already-ready older pull request.
findings.title: Refresh older ready evidence before using the train shortcut

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - The default branch moves while the combined check runs, so every affected member must take the individual-check path. The repaired helper asserts only `Closing`, the printed retest line and `merged`; the GitHub stub returns green and the test never checks that CI for each newly published head was read or could block the merge. A fallback that prints the retest line but merges before its new check finishes would pass. The standalone merge tests do not prove that the train fallback reaches that gate.
findings.title: Gate: prove each train fallback waits for its own CI

findings.body:
Gain 2, Work 1, Harm 1
When two changes are ready but one changes `forge.toml`, selection records its reason and then returns here because only one member remains. The recorded reasons are printed only by `_train`, so Forge silently falls back without naming the excluded change or why, contrary to the stated guide behavior.
findings.title: Follow-up: Report exclusions when fewer than two changes can join
